25 What is not a possible value for the wavelength of the named electromagnetic waves when it is
travelling in a vacuum?
electromagnetic
wave
wavelength / m
A
γ-rays
3 × 10–13
B
X-rays
3 × 10–10
C
infrared
3 × 10–6
D
microwaves
3 × 10–5

hints: Notice the wavelength order in a vacuum: $\gamma$-rays are shortest, then X-rays, then infrared, then microwaves are much longer.
Recall the boundary near $10^{-3} \text{ m}$: infrared is shorter than about $1 \text{ mm}$ while microwaves are longer than about $1 \text{ mm}$.
Compare $3 \times 10^{-5} \text{ m}$ with $10^{-3} \text{ m}$ and decide whether it belongs with infrared or with microwaves.
walkthrough: List the spectrum in order of increasing wavelength: $\gamma$-rays, X-rays, ultraviolet, visible, infrared, microwaves, radio waves.

Recall approximate vacuum ranges: $\gamma$-rays below about $10^{-11} \text{ m}$, X-rays about $10^{-13} \text{ m}$ to $10^{-8} \text{ m}$, infrared about $7 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$ to $10^{-3} \text{ m}$, microwaves about $10^{-3} \text{ m}$ to $10^{-1} \text{ m}$.
Check $3 \times 10^{-13} \text{ m}$ for $\gamma$-rays, $3 \times 10^{-10} \text{ m}$ for X-rays and $3 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}$ for infrared: each falls inside its named band.
Check $3 \times 10^{-5} \text{ m}$: it equals $0.03 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}$, which is about 30 times smaller than the $10^{-3} \text{ m}$ lower limit for microwaves.
Therefore $3 \times 10^{-5} \text{ m}$ is an infrared wavelength, not a microwave wavelength. This is option D.

A.explanation: Possible, as $3 \times 10^{-13} \text{ m}$ is in the very short wavelength region expected for $\gamma$-rays.

B.explanation: Possible, as $3 \times 10^{-10} \text{ m}$ lies in the typical X-ray range between $\gamma$-rays and ultraviolet.

C.explanation: Possible, as $3 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}$ is between about $10^{-3} \text{ m}$ and $7 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$, the infrared range.

D.explanation: Not possible, as $3 \times 10^{-5} \text{ m}$ is shorter than about $10^{-3} \text{ m}$ and so lies in the infrared region, not the microwave region.
